newsitem.title: ITALY: TIM slides on STET/Telecom merger comment.
newsitem.headline: TIM slides on STET/Telecom merger comment.

text.p: Shares in Italian mobile phone company Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) slipped after Posts Minister Antonio Maccanico said he did not rule out that TIM could be included in the planned STET -Telecom Italia merger.
At 1445 GMT, TIM shares were down 1.35 percent at 3,445 lire in volume of over 19 million shares, after the stock had been firmer in morning trade reaching a high of 3,550 lire.
Earlier this week, the Italian Treasury announced that the state-controlled telecoms holding group STET would be merged with telecoms operating company Telecom Italia.

"No-one has said that TIM will remain outside the merger," Maccanico said in reply to reporters' questions at a meeting in Rome. He added the aim of the merger is "to confer the greatest value on the biggest telephone operator which we have in Italy."

When the STET /Telecom Italia merger was announced on November 11, STET shares immediately rose as the company would lose its holding group status and become more attractive to international investors, while Telecom Italia shares slipped in response.
